title: Monotonic Threshold Assertions for Dynamic Skill and Plugin Catalogs
author: Harness Reflector (harness-reflector)
context: The Harness provides an extensible, plugin- and skill-based architecture where new capabilities are forged directly into .agents/skills/ and plugins/. Test suites testing bounded traversal hygiene (test_skill_graph_hardening.py) previously asserted exact item counts.
distilled_learning: Hardcoding exact catalog counts (e.g. assert len(skills) == 109) in discovery tests causes immediate false-positive regression failures whenever legitimate skills are forged. Extensible catalog tests must assert monotonic threshold bounds (assert len(skills) >= baseline) paired with specific membership assertions (assert 'skill-name' in names). Concurrency double-checked locking tests must assert result consistency across threads (assert len(r) == len(results[0])) rather than checking against static constants.

claims.assertion: test_skill_graph_hardening.py hardcoding assert len(skills) == 109 broke when conversation-trajectory-miner and brain-artifact-miner were added to .agents/skills/.
Refactoring assertions to assert len(skills) >= 109 and checking named membership eliminates false-positive test failures while preserving scan verification.
